lead.tldr: Kalshi's $22B valuation signals massive institutional appetite for regulated prediction markets, potential for new derivatives platforms • KelpDAO/LayerZero exploit triggers $290M loss, prompting tighter collateral standards across DeFi lending protocols • U.S. Treasury compliance demand on Binance raises operational risk, could limit global liquidity for U.S. traders • Core Scientific's $3.3B note funds AI‑focused data centers, signaling mining sector's shift toward compute services • Coinbase Q1 earnings miss highlights revenue volatility, growth now hinges on Base derivatives and stablecoin activity • Delayed CLARITY Act Senate markup prolongs stablecoin yield uncertainty, pressuring issuers to seek alternative regulatory pathways

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, Kalshi’s $22 billion valuation underscores the surge in prediction‑market investments while the KelpDAO/LayerZero breach froze $15 billion of DeFi TVL, prompting tighter collateral standards at Aave. Meanwhile, Binance faces a new U.S. Treasury compliance demand amid heightened regulatory scrutiny.

top_signals.title: Prediction Market Kalshi Achieves $22B Valuation on Coatue-Led Series F Raise on Bankless
top_signals.summary: Kalshi is a U.S. prediction‑market platform that recently completed a $1 billion Series F financing round led by Coatue Management. The new capital lifts the company’s valuation to $22 billion. The raise follows an 800% surge in institutional trading volume on the platform. With more than 90% of U.S. prediction‑market activity flowing through Kalshi, it is now the dominant player in the sector.

top_signals.title: KelpDAO/LayerZero Exploit Drains $290m, Freezes DeFi Markets
top_signals.summary: KelpDAO’s liquid restaking token rsETH was compromised in a hack that extracted $290 million by exploiting a misconfiguration in the LayerZero OFT bridge. The attacker then posted the stolen rsETH as collateral on major lending platforms Aave, Compound and Euler to borrow $236 million. These leveraged positions triggered rapid liquidations that froze trading activity across affected DeFi markets. The incident also contributed to a $15 billion reduction in total value locked across the DeFi ecosystem, highlighting systemic risk from bridge vulnerabilities.

top_signals.title: Binance Receives Compliance Demand from U.S. Treasury: The Information on Bankless
top_signals.summary: The U.S. Department of the Treasury has privately urged Binance to fully comply with an independent monitoring program tied to its 2023 guilty plea for money laundering and sanctions violations. The demand follows reports that more than $1 billion moved through Binance to entities linked to Iran. It arrives amid a Senate inquiry and a Department of Justice investigation into the exchange’s activities. Institutional investors should watch the regulatory outcome as it could impact Binance’s operational risk and market access.

top_signals.title: Core Scientific sold $208 million of bitcoin in Q1 as AI pivot continues
top_signals.summary: Core Scientific disclosed a $347.2 million loss for the first quarter while selling $208 million of Bitcoin to fund its transition to AI‑focused data center services. The company secured a $3.3 billion senior secured note offering to provide additional capital for the AI pivot. It also expanded its colocation agreement with CoreWeave to 590 megawatts of capacity. The expanded partnership is projected to generate $10.2 billion in revenue over the next twelve years, underscoring the strategic shift toward high‑performance AI infrastructure.

top_signals.title: Coinbase (COIN) news: weak crypto markets cause Q1 earnings miss
top_signals.summary: Coinbase, the leading U.S. cryptocurrency exchange, disclosed a surprise first‑quarter loss and missed revenue expectations, causing its shares to drop more than 5% in after‑hours trading. The earnings shortfall was driven by weaker trading volumes and lower subscription revenue amid a broader crypto market downturn. The firm nevertheless emphasized growth in derivatives, prediction‑market activity and stablecoin usage on its Base blockchain.

top_signals.title: One Year In: What Ripple's $25M Education Bet Made Possible
top_signals.summary: Ripple contributed $25 million, mainly in its RLUSD stablecoin, to the education nonprofits DonorsChoose and Teach For America. The $15 million portion directed to DonorsChoose supported more than 48,000 classroom projects across the United States. This initiative illustrates how a crypto‑native stablecoin can be deployed at scale for philanthropic purposes. Institutional investors may view the program as evidence of practical use cases for digital assets beyond trading and speculation.

top_signals.title: Stablecoin news: AI agents and large corporates will lead the next stablecoin boom
top_signals.summary: Executives from Bridge and Deus X Capital note that large corporations are increasingly adopting stablecoins to manage treasury functions and facilitate cross‑border payments. They also highlight that AI agents are poised to generate a new wave of micropayments, expanding the use cases for stablecoins. This momentum is expected to accelerate as payment‑focused blockchains such as Tempo, which receives backing from Stripe and Paradigm, enhance the underlying infrastructure, making stablecoin transactions more efficient for institutional participants.

top_signals.title: Aave to Tighten Collateral Standards Following Near-Disaster KelpDAO Crisis on Bankless
top_signals.summary: Aave Labs, the development arm of the Aave DeFi lending platform, is implementing a comprehensive overhaul of its collateral assessment framework. The changes introduce mandatory reviews of cybersecurity, interoperability and technical architecture for all assets accepted as collateral. The move follows the KelpDAO exploit that caused a $200M borrowing loss and exposed weaknesses in the protocol’s risk controls. By raising minimum collateral standards, Aave aims to lower future risk exposure for its lending markets and protect institutional participants.

top_signals.title: CLARITY Act 2026: Senate Banking Markup & Stablecoin Yield
top_signals.summary: The CLARITY Act, which cleared the House in July 2025, has moved to the Senate Banking Committee for markup. Lawmakers are still debating how the bill will address yield generation on stablecoins and the integration of decentralized finance provisions. The outcome of the markup will determine whether the legislation can secure the bipartisan support needed for timely passage. If the committee delays further, enactment could slip past 2026, limiting the act’s immediate influence on the crypto market and affecting institutional exposure to regulated digital assets.

top_signals.title: CZ floats Binance.US revival to give U.S. users access to global crypto liquidity
top_signals.summary: Binance founder Changpeng Zhao has floated the idea of reviving Binance.US to give U.S. traders access to deeper global crypto liquidity and better pricing. He said that restoring the U.S. platform would allow American users to tap the same order books and market depth that are available to Binance customers worldwide. Zhao also highlighted BNB Chain as the preferred payments rail for automated AI‑agent transactions, suggesting it could underpin the revived service. The proposal comes as recent improvements in U.S. crypto regulatory policy create a more favorable environment for such a relaunch.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin price news: BTC closing May over $76,000 would confirm bull market, Tom Lee says
top_signals.summary: Fundstrat analyst Tom Lee said that a May close above $76,000 would confirm the end of the crypto winter and signal a new bull market for Bitcoin. He highlighted that the next market cycle is likely to be driven by tokenization, AI‑driven finance and increasing stablecoin usage. Bitcoin is already trading near $80,000 and has posted a third consecutive monthly gain, underscoring the momentum that could attract institutional capital.

top_signals.title: U.S. added 115K jobs in April, nearly doubling expectations
top_signals.summary: The U.S. labor market added 115,000 jobs in April, nearly double the forecast and keeping the unemployment rate at 4.3 percent. The robust employment report arrived as Bitcoin fell below the $70,000 level. At the same time total value locked in decentralized finance reached its lowest point in 20 months, underscoring heightened macroeconomic pressure on crypto assets that institutional portfolios must monitor.
